gaps.why_now: The roadmap names an Architecture Council review process, but the live repo lacked a reviewable process note that says when council review is required and what packet it must carry.
A dedicated manifest keeps the new governance slice explicit and machine-checkable instead of burying the scope inside prose.
The Phase 15 review-process note should stay runnable so future edits do not quietly drop required trigger, packet, or decision-bucket language.
The live review checklist needed one explicit prompt that links freeze-map status-change requests back to the Architecture Council review record and decision bucket.
The shared Phase 15 build gate should run the review-process test alongside the existing freeze-map governance test so the governance lane stays coherent.
The landed Phase 15 parity scorecard is now the live evidence attachment point for Architecture Council requests instead of a planned follow-up.
The review-process packet now standardizes where each frozen anchor stores Council decision records, blocker dispositions, benchmark notes, and replay commands.
The review-process note now records the retained `retired_from_active_discussion` closeout state and the reopen triggers that keep a stay-in-C outcome reviewable without implying approval.
The review-process note now names the bounded reopen-trigger catalog so later exception records and scorecard updates reuse the same stay-in-C reopen vocabulary.
If a retained stay-in-C packet reopens because ownership or validation changed, the review record now has to refresh both the current lane owner and the rollback owner before active review resumes.

The shared review checklist now also has to keep the current roadmap phase and written rationale explicit, so those roadmap-backed review-process requirements do not live only in the survey note and manifest.
